items.name: The box-checker trap
items.seat_response: Name the pattern kindly, ask what the client is becoming beyond the checklist, and convert one box into a chosen step with a finish line.
signals: Every box checked and a flat, empty feeling about the work
Anxiety rises when a detail escapes control
Achievement is accumulating without a sense of direction
items.summary: The export's Becoming failure pattern: living as a meticulous box-checker, bent on achievement and control, which leads to emptiness and burnout.

items.name: Paralysis by not-enoughness
items.seat_response: Apply the Power of Small: define one finite, completable first step and bind it off before revisiting the whole.
signals: Nothing seems fixable or capable of being finished
The client rehearses their inadequacy instead of the task
Starting is deferred until confidence arrives
items.summary: The export's Light We Carry failure pattern: the size of the problem and the belief of not being enough stall the client before they start.

items.name: The fearful mind driving
items.seat_response: Run the danger-or-newness test out loud, separate documented risk from rehearsed catastrophe, and return the steering to preparation and evidence.
signals: Catastrophe rehearsal dominates the client's account
Decisions keep being made at the peak of dread
items.summary: The export's execution rule names the failure directly: the fearful mind cannot be evicted, but letting it seize the steering wheel starts the plummet.

items.name: Skipped preparation and optics blindness
items.seat_response: Stop the step, run the preparation pass for content and optics, and add a rehearsal plus a self-review loop before proceeding.
signals: The plan covers the message but not how it will be received or clipped
No rehearsal, no route run, no review of prior footage or feedback
items.summary: The export records the lesson learned from being cut up by opposition imagery: preparing only the content and not the optics leaves the client exposed, and amateurs wing what experts rehearse.

items.name: The fixed-identity belief
items.seat_response: Reframe with the becoming lens: ask who the client is in the process of becoming and which option keeps that process alive.
signals: The client speaks of themselves as a finished product, succeeding or failed for good
A setback is read as a verdict on who they are
External judgments have been internalized as self-perception limits
items.summary: The export's root cause of struggle in Becoming: believing identity is fixed, that one becomes something and that is the end, compounded by internalized external judgment.

items.name: Armor that does not fit
items.seat_response: Ask which protection the moment actually requires, lighten what alienates the client from themselves, and add support where they are genuinely exposed.
signals: Defensiveness so heavy it alienates the client from their own values
Or the opposite: no preparation and no boundaries, leaving the client exposed
Snapping at loved ones, excessive worry about uncontrollables, fear revving up (the export's internal red flags)
items.summary: The export's transformation arc describes armor that is either too heavy, alienating the self, or insufficient, leaving the person exposed, with internal red flags as the self-review signal.
